final_message:
I added all three views to `notebooks/explore.py`. `marimo check` passes, and the notebook runs from top to bottom with no cell errors.

No live marimo session was running for this notebook, so I edited the file directly instead of going through marimo-pair.

Each view has a hypothesis cell before it and a facts cell after it:

1. **`shipments_per_month`**: a line chart of monthly totals for Jan 2023 to Dec 2024, 1,199 shipments in all. Monthly totals range from 35 to 60. April to June came in at 54, 55 and 50 in 2023, and at 35, 41 and 39 in 2024.
2. **`q2_dip_by_port`**: a bar chart of each port's Q2 shipment count against its average for the other three quarters, with both years pooled. Ivelholm (−43%), Fennick (−35%) and Brackwater (−29%) are lowest. Cindervale (+23%) and Aldermouth (+13%) are above their average.
3. **`q2_dip_by_carrier_type`**: the same measure by carrier type. Tanker is −15%, container −14% and bulk −4%. Container ships make up 59% of all shipments.

I defined the "dip" as the Q2 count ÷ the average of the other three quarters, minus 1, with both years pooled. If you'd rather measure it another way, such as per year or by TEU instead of shipment count, I can switch it.

The facts cells only record the numbers. They're ready for your verdict on each hypothesis.

/tmp/mnb98/venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
p='notebooks/explore.py'
src=open(p).read()
cells='''

@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Hypothesis.** Shipments fall in the second quarter. Outcome: monthly totals for April to June sit below the months around them.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def shipments_per_month(mo, pl, shipments):
    import altair as alt

    _monthly = (
        shipments.group_by(pl.col('ship_date').dt.truncate('1mo').alias('month'))
        .agg(pl.len().alias('shipments'))
        .sort('month')
        .collect()
    )
    shipments_per_month = mo.ui.altair_chart(
        alt.Chart(_monthly)
        .mark_line(point=True)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X('month:T', title='Month'),
            y=alt.Y('shipments:Q', title='Shipments'),
            tooltip=['month:T', 'shipments:Q'],
        )
        .properties(title='Total shipments per month')
    )
    shipments_per_month
    return alt, shipments_per_month


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Facts.** 1,199 shipments over 24 months, Jan 2023 to Dec 2024. Monthly totals range from 35 (Apr 2024) to 60 (Mar 2023). Apr–Jun: 54, 55, 50 in 2023; 35, 41, 39 in 2024. Mar: 60 in 2023, 59 in 2024. Jul: 53 in 2023, 57 in 2024.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Hypothesis.** The second-quarter dip is concentrated in a few ports. Outcome: a handful of ports have Q2 counts well below their average for the other quarters, while the rest sit near zero.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def q2_dip_by_port(alt, mo, pl, shipments):
    _by_port = (
        shipments.with_columns(pl.col('ship_date').dt.quarter().alias('quarter'))
        .group_by('port')
        .agg(
            pl.col('quarter').eq(2).sum().alias('q2_shipments'),
            pl.col('quarter').ne(2).sum().truediv(3).alias('other_quarter_avg'),
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col('q2_shipments').truediv(pl.col('other_quarter_avg')).sub(1).alias('q2_dip')
        )
        .sort('q2_dip')
        .collect()
    )
    q2_dip_by_port = mo.ui.altair_chart(
        alt.Chart(_by_port)
        .mark_bar()
        .encode(
            x=alt.X('q2_dip:Q', title='Q2 vs. other-quarter average', axis=alt.Axis(format='%')),
            y=alt.Y('port:N', sort='x', title='Port'),
            tooltip=['port:N', 'q2_shipments:Q', alt.Tooltip('other_quarter_avg:Q', format='.1f'), alt.Tooltip('q2_dip:Q', format='.1%')],
        )
        .properties(title='Second-quarter dip by port (2023–2024 pooled)')
    )
    q2_dip_by_port
    return (q2_dip_by_port,)


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Facts.** Q2 vs. other-quarter average, both years pooled, 10 ports. Ivelholm −42.9% (20 vs. 35.0), Fennick −35.1% (24 vs. 37.0), Brackwater −29.4% (28 vs. 39.7), Dovesend −14.3%, Hollowmere −10.0%, Emberly Quay −2.8%, Juniper Reach −1.4%, Glassford +7.1%, Aldermouth +13.1% (46 vs. 40.7), Cindervale +22.9% (34 vs. 27.7).
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Hypothesis.** The second-quarter dip is driven by one carrier type. Outcome: one carrier type's Q2 count falls well below its other-quarter average, while the others hold steady.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def q2_dip_by_carrier_type(alt, mo, pl, shipments):
    _by_carrier = (
        shipments.with_columns(pl.col('ship_date').dt.quarter().alias('quarter'))
        .group_by('carrier_type')
        .agg(
            pl.col('quarter').eq(2).sum().alias('q2_shipments'),
            pl.col('quarter').ne(2).sum().truediv(3).alias('other_quarter_avg'),
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col('q2_shipments').truediv(pl.col('other_quarter_avg')).sub(1).alias('q2_dip')
        )
        .sort('q2_dip')
        .collect()
    )
    q2_dip_by_carrier_type = mo.ui.altair_chart(
        alt.Chart(_by_carrier)
        .mark_bar()
        .encode(
            x=alt.X('q2_dip:Q', title='Q2 vs. other-quarter average', axis=alt.Axis(format='%')),
            y=alt.Y('carrier_type:N', sort='x', title='Carrier type'),
            tooltip=['carrier_type:N', 'q2_shipments:Q', alt.Tooltip('other_quarter_avg:Q', format='.1f'), alt.Tooltip('q2_dip:Q', format='.1%')],
        )
        .properties(title='Second-quarter dip by carrier type (2023–2024 pooled)')
    )
    q2_dip_by_carrier_type
    return (q2_dip_by_carrier_type,)


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Facts.** Q2 vs. other-quarter average, both years pooled. Tanker −15.0% (36 vs. 42.3), container −13.7% (158 vs. 183.0), bulk −3.6% (80 vs. 83.0). Container carries 707 of 1,199 shipments (59%).
    """)
    return
'''
